spec_provided_observability.name: TRANSMIT ERROR COUNT
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Tracks transmitter-side error events; thresholds 96 (heavily-disturbed warning), 128 (error-passive), 256 (bus-off).

spec_provided_observability.name: RECEIVE ERROR COUNT
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Tracks receiver-side error events; threshold 128 → error-passive.

spec_provided_observability.name: ACK SLOT response
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Per-frame acknowledgment: transmitter samples ACK SLOT for dominant; absence is ACKNOWLEDGMENT ERROR.

spec_provided_observability.name: ERROR FLAG
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Active = 6 dominant bits (visible globally); Passive = 6 recessive bits.

spec_provided_observability.name: OVERLOAD FLAG
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Receiver-requested delay before next DATA/REMOTE FRAME; 6 dominant bits.

spec_provided_observability.name: 11-consecutive-recessive monitor
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Used for re-entry from bus-off and start-up synchronization.

self_check_mechanisms: Monitoring — transmitters compare bit levels driven to bus levels detected.
Bit Stuffing — detect 6 consecutive identical bits in stuffed fields = STUFF ERROR.
Message Frame Check — fixed-form fields (CRC DELIMITER, ACK DELIMITER, EOF, INTERMISSION) checked for illegal bits = FORM ERROR.

error_count_thresholds.consequence: Diagnostic warning — heavily disturbed bus (note in spec).

recovery_from_bus_off: After 128 occurrences of 11 consecutive recessive bits on the bus, a bus-off node is permitted to become error-active again (error counts both reset to 0).
notes: CAN 2.0 does not specify scan / JTAG / BIST. The protocol's strong built-in error detection (CRC + bit-monitoring + bit-stuffing + frame check + ACK) plus fault confinement counts provide a self-checking system at the protocol layer.
